## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Bhikkhāparamparajātaka* (Ja 496) is a canonical birth story in the Jātaka collection, positioned at the conclusion of the *Pakiṇṇakavagga* in the fourth volume of Fausböll's edition [Fausböll 1887]. According to its opening narrative framework, the Buddha related this discourse while residing at Jetavana concerning a faithful and devoted landowner (*kuṭumbika*) who continually offered hospitality and honor to the Buddha and the Saṅgha [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1887]. Modern scholarship highlights that the narrative sharply differentiates the *paccekabuddha* from the traditional Brahmanic ascetic (*tāpasa*), designed to demonstrate that among all social and religious dignitaries, the Buddhist monastic—embodied in the story by the *paccekabuddha*—is the preeminent recipient worthy of alms (*dakkhiṇeyya*) [Wiltshire 1990]. In the concluding identification of the birth story (*samodhāna*), the landowner is identified with the contemporary devotee, while past figures are linked to Ānanda (the king), Sāriputta (the royal priest), and the Bodhisatta (the Himalayan ascetic) [Fausböll 1887].
No external parallels are recorded for the text by SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus registers substantial Pali-internal text reuse with the commentary in the fourth volume of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* across 14 matching segments totaling 2,342 characters [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns short, low-scoring passages algorithmically with cross-language corpora, including the Tibetan *Vinayavastu* (D0001-4), the Chinese *Bieyi za ahan jing* (T 100), and the *Madhyamāgama* (T 26), although these represent machine matches rather than confirmed parallels [DharmaNexus].
